stem: A k-NN classifier uses Euclidean distance on two raw features, one measured in metres and one in millimetres. What should be checked before interpreting “nearest” as useful similarity?

options.text: Whether increasing k makes all distance-unit choices equivalent.
Whether feature scaling and the chosen metric reflect the task’s intended similarity.
Whether a numeric class label can be added to every test feature vector before measuring distance.
Whether the largest raw numeric feature should always dominate, regardless of its unit.

assumptions: Added mixed-unit example; no claim that a particular scaling method is always optimal.

stem: A NumPy array is explicitly created with dtype=object and stores the Python values 1 and "red". Which statement correctly qualifies the assignment’s array-versus-DataFrame comparison?

options.text: The array still has one array dtype, object, while its referenced Python objects can have different types; DataFrame columns can each have their own dtype.
The array must have two separate top-level array dtypes because its Python objects differ.
Creating an object array forces every stored object to become a floating-point number.
A DataFrame must convert all columns to the same dtype whenever one column contains text.

assumptions: Added object-array counterexample; structured dtypes also require care, but no claim that every array stores one primitive numeric type is made.
